sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (match the columns, true/false, fill in the blanks or one-word answers).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) The early childhood centre administrator is responsible for the overall operation of the centre and its services. (ii) Laissez-faire is the most controlling management style.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False — autocratic is the most controlling; laissez-faire is the least.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Financial management deals with procurement and ________ of funds. (ii) The focus of ________ auditing is to establish the truth and fairness of the accounts.
questions.answer: (i) allocation (ii) external

questions.q: Match: (a) Supervision (b) Mentor focuses on — (i) Mentee's total development (ii) Continuous review of the programme (iii) Monitoring staff performance and helping them improve
Answer in one sentence: (i) Rupinder is an ECCE centre head. Mention one major role she would undertake. (ii) What are the two types of auditing?
questions.answer: (i) Any one: day-to-day management; supervising, mentoring and monitoring staff; ensuring children's safety; maintaining records; managing finances and resources; working with parents and the community. (ii) Internal auditing and external auditing.

questions.q: Answer in one word: (i) The principal book with debit and credit columns for each account. (ii) The statement listing all assets and liabilities of a centre.
questions.answer: (i) Ledger (ii) Balance sheet

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What are the key functions shared by both management and administration?
questions.answer: Both are concerned with planning, organising and controlling — and with directing resources and people towards the goals of the ECCE centre.

or.q: What are the three levels of management typically found in an ECCE centre?
or.answer: Top level — the owners of the centre; middle level — the centre head and assistants; first level — the ECCE staff and teachers.

questions.q: What is the role of the head of an ECCE centre in supervision, mentoring and monitoring?
questions.answer: As supervisor the head checks staff performance and helps them improve; as mentor she acts as a friend, guide and role model; as monitor she checks overall and individual progress, identifies problems and advises solutions.

or.q: What are the benefits of supervision in an ECCE centre?
or.answer: It fills gaps in teachers' knowledge and skills, helps understand ground realities and solve problems, motivates teachers, builds the team, makes teachers aware of new guidelines and helps them relate to the community.

questions.q: Why is it necessary to document and keep records for all children? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: Any two: records build a picture of each child; they monitor progress in all domains and help plan the next steps; they show the gap between expected and actual learning; they help communicate with parents and the next school; they show accountability.

or.answer: Personal details of each child with academic performance, assessments and results; school policies; minutes of meetings and information from the education department and other bodies; also admission registers, roll books, progress reports, staff, financial and stock records.

questions.q: What are stock records?
questions.answer: Records of all resources and materials at the centre — outdoor and indoor equipment, furniture, and learning materials such as story books, blocks, puzzles, crayons and paper — showing the quantity in store and the amount used; they are updated regularly.

questions.q: What are the two types of auditing?
questions.answer: Internal auditing — regular, frequent checking of the centre's transactions and records to see they follow the budget and set procedures. External auditing — an outside check that establishes the truth and fairness of the accounts and their compliance with statutes.

questions.q: What is a ledger?
questions.answer: The principal book or computer file of a centre for recording and totalling its economic transactions, with separate debit and credit columns and an opening and closing balance for each account.
questions.note: October 2021 asked for a one-sentence explanation.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Why are cumulative records important? Describe a proforma for a cumulative record for children.
questions.answer: A cumulative record (child's profile), compiled with parents at admission, builds a full picture of each child, helps plan for the child's needs, track progress and communicate with parents and the next school. Proforma: name of the child; date of birth; sex; position in the family; number of siblings; father's name, qualification and occupation; mother's name, qualification and occupation; address and contact number; immunisation status; allergies, if any; specific needs of the child; any other relevant information.

questions.q: What are the different types of records maintained in an ECCE centre?
questions.answer: Children's records (profile/cumulative record, attendance register, checklists, portfolio, progress reports, observations); staff records (personal details, qualifications, job description, salary, training, attendance); stock records (equipment, furniture, learning materials); financial records (cash book, ledger, balance sheet, fees, receipts, bank records); miscellaneous records (safety inspection book, menu, log books, prospectus, PTA minutes, visitor's book, photographs).

questions.q: Differentiate between a cash book, a ledger and a balance sheet.
questions.answer: Cash book: a record of small, day-to-day purchases (stationery, cleaning material, ration) kept by a staff member before they are posted to the ledger. Ledger: the principal book or file recording and totalling all transactions, with debit and credit columns and opening and closing balances for each account. Balance sheet: a statement of the centre's financial position listing assets (current and long-term, such as cash, furniture, building) and then liabilities (current, such as salaries; long-term, such as loans).

questions.q: Explain the importance of accounting and social auditing.
questions.answer: Social accounting and auditing record and report the social and environmental effects of an organisation's economic actions to interest groups and society. It checks performance against social, environmental and economic objectives and values. Objectives: effective use of resources; an ongoing record of how the centre has changed; feedback on how things are going; knowing what works well and what does not; knowing how far aims are achieved; and collecting information for grant applications and reports.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss the importance of supervision, mentoring and monitoring in the management of an ECCE centre.
questions.answer: These sustain and improve the quality of services; the National ECCE Policy, 2013 asks for a systematic monitoring framework with input, output and outcome indicators, and the centre head plays all three roles. Supervision: monitoring staff performance, noting merits and shortcomings and helping them improve; it fills skill gaps, helps solve ground problems, motivates teachers, builds the team, spreads new guidelines, checks materials and the environment, gives feedback and professional support, and identifies training needs. Monitoring: continuous review of implementation with regular data collection; it checks whether inputs are well used and activities are on time, finds and solves problems, and adapts the programme to the changing needs of children and families. Mentoring: a trusting partnership of mutual benefit; the mentor helps on specific issues, coaches skills, shares resources, challenges the mentee, creates a safe space to take risks and focuses on total development.
questions.note: October 2022 also asked for the benefits of supervision.

questions.q: Why are mobilisation and utilisation of resources important for an ECCE centre? Explain ways to raise funds.
questions.answer: All enterprises need funds, and expenses keep rising; a centre must raise enough money for building or rent, staff, materials, food and play equipment, and use it well through a budget, prompt records, monthly reviews and audits so that funds serve their purpose. Ways to raise funds: (1) grant-in-aid and mini-grants from government ministries and departments such as the Ministry of Women and Child Development and the Social Welfare Board; (2) fairs and cultural functions selling articles made by children and parents; (3) volunteerism — skilled parents and community members teach or make learning materials and toys; (4) renting out the space after centre hours for dance or art classes, or growing vegetables to sell; (5) donation camps for toys, clothes, stationery and food grains; (6) donations and fees from parents and other donors.
questions.note: April 2022 asked: describe the management and utilisation of funds in the context of ECCE.
